newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina serial killer gets nine death sentences.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina serial killer gets nine death sentences.

text.p: Convicted serial killer Henry Louis Wallace was given nine death sentences on Wednesday -- one for each woman he confessed to strangling.
The jury returned the recommendation of death after deliberating under "appropriate tension" for four days, the jury foreman said.
"We looked at each case, one at a time, and would have been prepared to bring in different recommendations for each," said foreman Robbie Grier, a 42-year-old advertising salesman.
"The (death sentence) was one you had to make, but nobody was anxious to make," he added.
On Jan. 7 the same jury rejected Wallace's mental illness defence and found him guilty of nine counts of first-degree murder, eight counts of first-degree rape and other charges.
Family members could not contain their feelings as the clerk read the death verdict in Mecklenburg Superior Court.
"Yes!," shouted Judy Williams, a close friend of the family of victim Shawna Hawk, before collapsing in tears.
Hawk's mother Dee Sumpter sobbed and said afterward: "I feel a sense of tremendous relief."

Hawk, like the other women, was raped and killed in her home. Each of the victims killed during Wallace's 22-month killing spree which ended in March 1994, knew him as a co-worker at area fastfood restuarants or as an acquaintance of his girlfriend.
Dressed in an ivory crewneck sweater and green khaki pants, Wallace, 31, sat with clasped hands pressed against his chin while jurors confirmed the death recommendations later imposed by the court.
"The prisoner Henry Louis Wallace ... is hereby sentenced to death," Superior Court Judge Robert Johnston said nine times. "May God have mercy on your soul."
Wallace, who did not testify in either phase of his trial, read an apology letter to family members.
"What words, in any language, can I say that will bring you comfort, quiet the storm, or release you from the mental prison I have put you in?" he asked in a clear, strong voice.
"I'm sorry? I apologise? I didn't mean to do it? I profess that all of these words, and all that I know, fall far short of what's needed to console any of you."

Several family members were clearly irritated by Wallace's comments, interrupting him by shouting questions of their own, and the sister of victim Caroline Love jumped from her seat screaming "you bastard" as she charged toward Wallace. She was in tears as sheriff's deputies escorted her from the court.
Other family members sat stone-faced as Wallace tried to solicit foregiveness by reciting a Bible verse about Christ's unending forgiveness.
Rev. Alfonso Slaughter, whose daughter Debra was choked with a towel and stabbed, said afterward he could forgive.
"I cannot stand up and tell people that God forgives all and (then) not forgive this man," Slaughter said.
The chief evidence against Wallace was his own audio-taped confession to police, in which Wallace detailed raping and strangling the women.
